_comment: HDFC Bank — Real-world profile derived from FY2025 Annual Report & Q4FY25 Earnings (year ended March 31, 2025)
_source: HDFC Bank Q4FY25 Earnings Presentation, toptradetrends.com FY25 analysis, Business Standard Q4FY25
_note_balance_sheet: Total Assets Rs 39,10,200 cr (post HDFC Ltd merger July 2023). Gross Advances Rs 26,43,500 cr (+5.4% YoY); Total Deposits Rs 27,14,700 cr (+14.1% YoY). LDR ~96.5% — elevated due to inherited HDFC Ltd mortgage book funded by borrowings not deposits. Largest private sector bank in India by assets.
_note_deposits: CASA = 30.5% of deposits (Rs 8.29 lakh cr / Rs 27.14 lakh cr) — significantly lower than pre-merger ~42% due to HDFC Ltd not having a CASA franchise. Term deposits grew 20% YoY while CASA grew only 5.7%. Current ~11%, Savings ~19.5%, Term ~69.5%.
_note_exposure: Post-HDFC Ltd merger, home loans dominate at ~32% of advances (HDFC Ltd book). Retail other (personal/auto/kisan/credit card) ~30%, SME+commercial & rural ~20%, corporate/wholesale ~18%. Retail grew 9% YoY, commercial & rural 12.8%, corporate 3.6%.
_note_credit_quality: GNPA 1.33% (Mar 2025), improved from 1.42% in Dec 2024 but up from 1.24% in Mar 2024 — post-merger portfolio integration effects. Ex-agriculture GNPA 1.13%. Net NPA 0.43%. Strong underwriting but mortgage book seasoning ongoing.
_note_pnl: NIM 3.46% (lower than ICICI — home loans carry lower rates than unsecured/SME). ROA 1.94%. Cost-income 39.8% (best-in-class efficiency). Full-year PAT ~Rs 65,000 cr. ROE ~18%.
_note_capital: CRAR 19.6%, CET1 17.2% as of March 2025 — highest among large Indian banks. Reflects HDFC Ltd's strong capital base absorbed at merger plus strong internal accrual at 1.94% ROA.
